AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by total mesorectal excision (TME) surgery for locally advanced rectal cancer has been shown to improve local control and reduce toxicity, as compared to adjuvant CRT. We report the outcomes of our patients with locally advanced rectal cancer treated at National University Hospital, Singapore.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: From April 2002 to December 2014, 117 patients with T3/4, N0/+, M0 rectal cancer received neoadjuvant CRT followed by TME surgery. The treatment regimen comprised a total radiotherapy dose of 50.4 Gy in 28 daily fractions delivered concurrently with 5-fluorouracil or capecitabine chemotherapy over 5.5 weeks. All patients were planned for TME surgery. Local control, disease-free survival, overall survival and treatment toxicities were analysed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Median follow-up was 34 (range 2-122) months. 11.5% (n = 13/113) of patients achieved a pathological complete response (pCR) and 71.8% (n = 84/117) had either tumour or nodal downstaging following neoadjuvant CRT. 5.2% (n = 5/96) of patients had grade 3 acute toxicities (dermatitis and diarrhoea) and 3.1% (n = 3/96) had grade 3 late toxicities (fistula and strictures). There was no grade 4 toxicity noted. The five-year local recurrence rate, disease-free survival and overall survival were 4.5%, 65.7% and 80.6%, respectively. Multivariate analysis showed that nodal positivity was a predictor of poor disease-free survival and overall survival. Tumour downstaging and pCR did not improve outcomes.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Our outcomes were comparable to internationally published data and this treatment regimen remains the standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer in our local population.
